text: We evaluated a learned noisy-channel model of weak-label errors refined by expectation-maximization, using one EM round, with pythia-410m as the weak supervisor and qwen2.5-7b as the strong student, across 6 seeds. The weak model reaches 0.57 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling is 0.74, while the strong student trained on weak labels through this method attains a transfer accuracy of 0.58 with a standard error of 0.01. The resulting performance gap recovered is 0.03 with a standard error of 0.03, compared with a baseline PGR of 0.07. The method therefore does not recover more of the gap than the baseline; the measured PGR falls below it, and its standard error is as large as the point estimate itself, so the data do not support any claim of a gain. With only 6 seeds and a single EM round, these numbers should be read as preliminary, and further rounds or seeds would be needed to characterize the method's behavior.
